sub: Named after al-Aḥqāf, the sand dunes where Hūd warned ʿĀd (ayah 21)
theme: A reply to Makkah’s denial: the Qurʾān is from Allah, idols have no proof, and the resurrection is real. ʿĀd’s ruin warns the proud, believing jinn shame the deniers, and the Prophet ﷺ is told to be patient.
story: Revealed in Makkah around the end of the tenth year of prophethood, the “year of sorrow”. A three-year boycott had just ended, then the Prophet ﷺ lost his uncle Abū Ṭālib and his wife Khadījah. The Quraysh grew even harsher.

He went to Ṭāʾif to invite its people and was chased out and pelted with stones. On the way back, reportedly at Nakhlah, a group of jinn heard him reciting the Qurʾān in prayer, believed, and went home to warn their people (29–32).

The surah answers Makkah’s objections: that life has no purpose, that idols deserve worship, that the Qurʾān is invented, that the weak believing first proves it false, and that no one is raised again. People ran from the message, but jinn believed.

sections.title: Allah sent the Book; idols created nothing; it’s no magic or forgery
sections.meaning: The Book comes from Allah, and the universe was made with purpose and a fixed end, yet deniers turn away. Their idols created nothing and have no scripture or knowledge behind them. They call the Qurʾān magic or forgery; the Prophet ﷺ answers that he is no new messenger and only follows revelation.
points: Ḥā Mīm; the Book is from Allah; creation has purpose and an end
Show me what they created, or a scripture, or a trace of knowledge
No one is more astray; on that Day idols become enemies
They call it magic, or forged; Allah is witness between us
I am no new messenger, and I follow only revelation
sections.matters: It lays the ground for the whole surah: the Book is from Allah, the world has a purpose, and worship is for Allah alone. The deniers’ charges (magic, forgery, something new) are each met with a demand for proof.
sections.story: No specific incident for 1–8; they answer Makkah calling the Qurʾān magic and invention. Ayah 9 has reports: a dream of a land to migrate to, or the pagans gloating that he didn’t know his own fate.
explained: Ḥā Mīm. The Book comes from al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm, the Mighty, the Wise. Allah made the heavens and earth bil-ḥaqq, with truth and purpose, not as play, and for a fixed term that ends on the Day of Resurrection. Yet the deniers turn away from what they are warned about.

So the challenge: show what your idols created, bring a scripture, or any trace of prophetic knowledge. They have none. The idols can’t hear, and on that Day they turn into enemies. Nor is the Qurʾān magic or forgery: had he forged it, no one could shield him from Allah. He is no new messenger, and follows only revelation.
teaches: Creation has a purpose, so life is not a game.
Beliefs about Allah need proof: revelation or sound reason, not habit.
What people worship besides Allah will abandon them when it matters most.
Even the Prophet ﷺ spoke about the unseen only from revelation.
sections.hook: Juz 26 begins here. Ayat 1–2 match the opening of Al-Jāthiyah (45) word for word. Ayah 4 demands proof in order: what they created → a scripture → a trace of knowledge.

sections.title: A witness believed, deniers sneered; those who stand firm get Paradise
sections.meaning: What if the Qurʾān is from Allah and you reject it, while a witness from the Children of Israel believed? The proud sneer that the weak got there first and call it an old lie. Yet Mūsā’s Book came before it, and those who stand firm on “Our Lord is Allah” win Paradise.
points: If it’s from Allah and a witness believed, while you were proud?
“Had it been good, they wouldn’t have beaten us to it”
Mūsā’s Book came first; this Book confirms it, in Arabic
Say “Our Lord is Allah,” stand firm: no fear, no grief
sections.matters: It exposes the real reason for rejection: not a lack of evidence but pride. Earlier scripture backs the Qurʾān, and against the deniers’ sneering it sets out the simple way to success: faith, then staying firm.
sections.story: Ayah 10 is reportedly about ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, though he accepted Islam later, in Madinah. Ayah 11 has several reports: the Quraysh mocking poor Muslims like Bilāl and ʿAmmār, or a believing slave-girl, or tribes outpaced by humbler ones.
explained: Think it through: suppose the Qurʾān is from Allah, and a witness from the Children of Israel recognised it and believed, while you turned away in pride. Arrogance toward the truth is wrongdoing, and Allah does not guide wrongdoers. The deniers’ excuse was snobbery: if this were good, the poor and weak wouldn’t have reached it before us.

Having missed its guidance, they call it an old lie. But the Qurʾān isn’t new or strange: Mūsā’s Book came before it as a guide and mercy, and this Book confirms it in clear Arabic. It warns wrongdoers and brings good news to those who do good: say “Our Lord is Allah,” stay firm, and Paradise is yours forever.
teaches: Pride, not lack of proof, is what usually blocks people from the truth.
Don’t judge the truth by who accepted it first.
When you miss out on something good, don’t belittle it.
Faith needs istiqāmah: saying it, then staying firm for life.
sections.hook: Ayat 7 and 11 pair up: hādhā siḥrun mubīn, then hādhā ifkun qadīm. Kitāb comes twice in 12: kitābu Mūsā, then kitābun muṣaddiq. Page 503 ends with ayah 14.

sections.title: Be good to parents: the grateful forty-year-old versus the child saying uff
sections.meaning: Allah commands kindness to parents, recalling the mother’s hardship. A grateful believer at forty prays for himself, his parents and children, and repents; Allah accepts his best deeds. The opposite child scorns his pleading parents and the resurrection, and joins the losers. Deniers are told they used up their pleasures in this world.
points: Kindness to parents; the mother’s hardship; the prayer at forty
Best deeds accepted, bad ones overlooked: a true promise
“Uff to you both”: mocks the resurrection, joins lost nations
Everyone has ranks by deeds, and no one is wronged
Before the Fire: you used up your good things already
sections.matters: After tawḥīd and standing firm comes kindness to parents, as so often in the Qurʾān. The two sons show that how you treat your parents and how you answer Allah go together, and that pleasures chased here can cost the Hereafter.
sections.story: Ayah 15 is reportedly about Abū Bakr, whose parents and children all accepted Islam; other reports name Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. Some linked ayah 17 to a son of Abū Bakr before Islam, but ʿĀʾishah denied it: it describes any undutiful denier.
explained: His mother carried and delivered him with kurh, hardship. Pregnancy and weaning take thirty months, and since weaning is up to two years, the shortest pregnancy is six months. At full strength and forty he prays: help me thank You for Your favours on me and my parents, do deeds You love, and make my children righteous. I repent.

Allah accepts the best of such people’s deeds and overlooks their faults. The opposite son snaps “uff” at parents begging Allah for his guidance, mocks rising from the grave, and calls it old legends. He joins earlier lost nations. Each side has ranks, and deniers will hear: you used up your good things in the world, so today, humiliation.
teaches: Remember your mother’s hardship and repay it with kindness.
Forty is a time to renew repentance and put the Hereafter first.
Pray for your parents and your children, not just yourself.
Rudeness to parents who call you to good is a double wrong.
Don’t use up all your good things in this world.
sections.hook: Two sons, two sayings: qāla rabbi awziʿnī (15) and qāla li-wālidayhi uff (17). Ulāʾika follows each (16, 18). Page 504 holds exactly 15–20. Ayah 20’s opening returns in 34.

sections.title: Hūd warns ʿĀd; they mistake the destroying wind for rain; idols fail
sections.meaning: Hūd warned ʿĀd at the sand dunes to worship Allah alone. They dared him to bring the punishment. A cloud came toward their valleys and they cheered for rain, but it was a wind that left only their homes standing. They were stronger than Makkah, yet nothing, not even their idols, saved them.
points: Remember ʿĀd’s brother, warning at al-Aḥqāf: worship only Allah
“Bring what you threaten!” Only Allah knows when; I just deliver
“A rain cloud!” No: a wind that left only their homes
More power than you, with hearing, sight and hearts, yet useless
Towns around you destroyed; their idols vanished when needed
sections.matters: Makkah was rushing the same punishment and trusting the same kind of gods. The ruins of ʿĀd and other nations around Arabia show that power and intelligence can’t protect those who reject Allah’s signs. It also consoles the Prophet ﷺ.
sections.story: No specific incident. Allah tells the story to console the Prophet ﷺ over his people’s rejection and to warn Makkah. Seeing clouds, the Prophet ﷺ would grow uneasy, remembering that ʿĀd had called their punishment “a cloud bringing us rain.”
explained: Hūd, their brother, warned ʿĀd among the sand dunes of al-Aḥqāf: worship only Allah, I fear a terrible Day for you. Other warners had come before and after him. They answered: have you come to turn us from our gods? Then bring it, if you’re truthful. Hūd replied that only Allah knows when; his task was to deliver.

Suffering drought, they saw a dark cloud heading for their valleys and rejoiced. It was the wind they had asked for, destroying everything by its Lord’s command until only their homes were left. ʿĀd were more firmly established than Makkah, with hearing, sight and minds, yet none of it helped. Towns around Makkah fell too, and their gods simply vanished.
teaches: Never dare Allah to bring His punishment.
Not everything that looks like a blessing is one.
Intelligence and power are useless if you reject Allah’s signs.
False gods disappear exactly when they are needed.
Learn from the ruins of those who came before.
sections.hook: It starts at the ۞ and fills page 505 (21–28). ʿĀriḍ comes twice in 24. Ayah 26 names hearing, sight, hearts twice. The word ifk links 11, 22 (li-taʾfikanā) and 28 (ifkuhum).

sections.title: Jinn listen silently to the Qurʾān, then warn their people to respond
sections.meaning: Allah sent a small group of jinn to hear the Qurʾān. They hushed each other, listened to the end, and went home as warners: we heard a Book after Mūsā that guides to truth. Answer Allah’s caller and be forgiven; whoever refuses cannot escape Allah and has no protector.
points: Jinn turned to you: “Listen quietly!” Then they went back as warners
A Book after Mūsā, confirming, guiding to truth and a straight path
Answer Allah’s caller: forgiveness and safety from painful punishment
Refuse, and there’s no escape and no protector: clear error
sections.matters: While people in Makkah and Ṭāʾif rejected the Prophet ﷺ, jinn believed after one hearing. It shames the deniers, comforts the Prophet ﷺ, and shows that his message reached jinn as well as humans.
sections.story: Reportedly, jinn barred from eavesdropping on heaven searched for the cause and found the Prophet ﷺ reciting in prayer at Nakhlah, either at Fajr on the way to ʿUkāẓ market or at night returning from Ṭāʾif. He didn’t see them; Allah told him.
explained: Allah turned a small group of jinn toward the Prophet ﷺ. Hearing the Qurʾān, they told each other anṣitū, “hush, listen!” When it ended, they had believed, and they went back to their people as warners. Later, jinn came to him in delegation after delegation.

Their message: we heard a Book sent down after Mūsā, confirming earlier scripture, guiding to truth in belief and a straight path in action. Answer Allah’s caller and believe, and He will forgive your sins and save you from painful punishment. Whoever refuses can’t escape Allah on earth, has no protector, and is clearly lost.
teaches: Listen to the Qurʾān in silence and with attention.
When you learn the truth, share it with your own people.
Call to Allah with both hope and warning.
If jinn believed after one hearing, no one has an excuse to ignore it.
sections.hook: Page 506 starts with ayah 29. Fa-lammā comes twice in 29: ḥaḍarūhu, then quḍiya. Yā qawmanā comes in 30 and opens 31. Dāʿiya Allāh comes in 31 (ajībū) and 32 (lā yujib).

sections.title: The heavens’ Creator raises the dead; deniers meet the Fire; be patient
sections.meaning: Allah created the heavens and earth without tiring, so He can surely bring the dead to life. At the Fire, deniers admit it is real, too late. So the Prophet ﷺ must be patient like the resolute messengers and not rush their punishment. On that Day, their whole life will feel like an hour.
points: He made the heavens and earth untired; He can raise the dead
“Isn’t this real?” “Yes, by our Lord.” “Then taste it.”
Be patient like the resolute; life will seem an hour of a day
sections.matters: It ties the surah together: the creation argument from the opening returns as proof of resurrection, the scene at the Fire repeats, and the Prophet ﷺ, in his year of grief, is told to hold on as the greatest messengers did.
sections.story: No specific incident; it closes the surah’s reply to Makkah. One report says ayah 35 came on the day of Uḥud, telling the Prophet ﷺ to be patient, though the surah is counted as Makkan.
explained: Can’t they see? The One who made the heavens and earth without tiring can easily give life to the dead. Balā, yes, He can do anything. Then the scene returns: deniers are brought before the Fire and asked, “Isn’t this real?” Now they swear, “Yes, by our Lord,” but it’s too late: taste the punishment for denying.

So be patient as ulū al-ʿazm were: Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā, or, by another view, all the messengers. Don’t rush their punishment; it is coming. When they see it, their life on earth will feel like one hour of a day. This is balāgh, a message delivered, and only the defiantly disobedient are destroyed.
teaches: Look at creation, and the resurrection becomes easy to believe.
Admit the truth now; admitting it later won’t help.
Patience is the way of the greatest messengers.
However long life feels, it will seem like an hour.
sections.hook: The close echoes earlier ayat: 33 has khalaqa as-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ (as in 3); 34 opens word for word like 20: wa yawma yuʿraḍu alladhīna kafarū ʿalā an-nār. Balā comes in 33 and 34.

groups.text: Ḥā Mīm. The Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. Creation has a purpose and a fixed end, but deniers turn away.
Show what your idols created, or any scripture or knowledge. They can’t answer, and on that Day they turn into enemies.
They call the Qurʾān magic, or say he forged it. If he had, no one could protect him from Allah.
He is no new messenger, follows only what is revealed, and is just a clear warner.
If it is from Allah and a witness from the Children of Israel believed while you were proud, you are the wrongdoers.
They sneer that the weak believed first and call it an old lie. Mūsā’s Book came before; this one confirms it.
Those who say “Our Lord is Allah” and stay firm: no fear, no grief, and Paradise forever.
Kindness to parents and the mother’s hardship. At forty the grateful believer prays and repents; Allah accepts his best deeds.
A son says “uff” to his believing parents and mocks the resurrection. He joins the lost nations before him.
Everyone has ranks by their deeds. Deniers at the Fire: you used up your pleasures, so today, humiliation.
Hūd warns ʿĀd at the dunes. They dare him to bring the punishment; he says only Allah knows when.
They took the approaching cloud for rain. It was a wind that destroyed everything but their homes.
They were more established than Makkah, with hearing, sight and minds, yet nothing and no idol saved them.
Jinn hear the Qurʾān in silence, then tell their people: a Book after Mūsā that guides to the truth.
Answer Allah’s caller and be forgiven. Whoever refuses can’t escape Him and has no protector.
The Creator of the heavens can raise the dead. At the Fire, deniers finally say “Yes, by our Lord.”
Be patient like the resolute messengers. Life will seem an hour. Only the defiantly disobedient are destroyed.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: separate letters that open the surah. Allah knows best what they mean. The safest course is not to guess, while being sure they were not sent without wisdom.

2.explain: Tanzīl al-kitāb: the Book is sent down from Allah, al-ʿAzīz, Mighty in His rule, and al-Ḥakīm, Wise in what He says and does. So reflect on it and be guided by it.

3.explain: Bil-ḥaqq: creation has a purpose, not idle play, and a fixed term that ends at the Resurrection. The One who made all this can bring people back. Still, the deniers turn away from the warning.

4.explain: Three demands for proof: what did your idols create on earth, or share in the heavens? Or bring a scripture, or athārah min ʿilm, a trace of knowledge handed down from earlier prophets.

5.explain: No one is more lost than someone who calls on idols that won’t answer until the Resurrection, meaning never. They don’t even know they are being called; they are lifeless.

6.explain: When people are gathered, those idols become their enemies and deny they were ever worshipped. What they relied on abandons them when they need it most.

7.explain: When the clear āyāt are recited, the deniers call the truth that has reached them siḥrun mubīn, obvious magic. Calling the truth magic turns reality upside down.

8.explain: Iftarāhu: “he made it up.” The reply: if I did, you couldn’t protect me from Allah’s punishment. He knows what you say and is witness enough. Al-Ghafūr ar-Raḥīm: the door to repentance is still open.

9.explain: Bidʿ: something new. Many messengers came before him. He doesn’t know what will happen to him or to them, except what Allah reveals. He follows only revelation and is a clear warner.
9.why: Reportedly, when persecution grew, the Prophet ﷺ dreamed of a land of palms to migrate to; asked when, he was silent, and this ayah came. Another report: the pagans gloated over it until 48:2 was revealed.

10.explain: Araʾaytum: think, what if the Qurʾān is from Allah and you reject it, while a witness from the Children of Israel testified to it and believed, and you were proud? Allah doesn’t guide such wrongdoers.
10.why: Reportedly about ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, a Jewish scholar who accepted Islam. Since the surah is Makkan and he became Muslim in Madinah, it is either a prophecy of him, a Madinan ayah placed here, or about Mūsā and the Torah.

11.explain: The deniers sneer: if it were any good, these people wouldn’t have reached it before us. Having missed its guidance, they call it ifkun qadīm, an old lie, as if copied from ancient peoples.
11.why: Reports differ on who “these people” were: poor Muslims like Bilāl, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb and Khabbāb; Zunairah, a slave-girl who accepted Islam; humbler tribes who converted before proud ones; or ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions.

12.explain: Before it came the Book of Mūsā, a guide to follow and a mercy. The Qurʾān confirms the earlier books in clear Arabic, to warn wrongdoers and give good news to al-muḥsinīn, those who do good.

13.explain: Rabbunā Allāh thumma istaqāmū: they declared Allah their Lord, then stayed firm on it all their lives. No fear about what lies ahead, and no grief over what they left behind.
13.why: Reportedly revealed about Abū Bakr, but its promise covers everyone who stays firm.

14.explain: They are the people of Paradise, living there forever as a reward for what they used to do. Their deeds are the means by which they reach Allah’s mercy.

15.explain: An emphatic command to treat parents with iḥsān. Kurhan: the mother carries and delivers with hardship; pregnancy and weaning total thirty months. At full strength and forty, he prays to be grateful, do good, have righteous children, and repents.
15.why: Reportedly about Abū Bakr, who prayed this at forty, freed nine tortured believers, and saw his parents and children all accept Islam. Another report names Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, whose mother refused food until he left Islam. The command is general.

16.explain: Allah accepts the best of what they did and overlooks their misdeeds, counting them among the people of Paradise. Waʿd aṣ-ṣidq: a true promise from the One who never breaks His word.

17.explain: Uff: a word of disgust. His parents urge faith; he mocks: will I be raised from the grave when whole generations died? They cry to Allah for him: “Woe to you, believe!” He says: old legends.
17.why: Some linked it to a son of Abū Bakr before he accepted Islam. ʿĀʾishah denied this, and ayah 18 dooms the one described, while he became an excellent Muslim. So it describes any undutiful son who denies the resurrection.

18.explain: Ḥaqqa ʿalayhim al-qawl: the word of punishment is due on them, alongside earlier nations of jinn and humans who died denying. They are khāsirīn: they lost their very capital, faith.

19.explain: Darajāt: everyone has ranks by what they did. The levels of Paradise rise and the levels of the Fire sink. Each is paid in full: no good deed reduced, no bad deed added.

20.explain: Deniers brought before the Fire hear: you used up your good things in worldly life and enjoyed them. Today’s punishment is al-hūn, humiliation, for arrogance without right and disobedience. Fearing this ayah, ʿUmar held back from luxuries.

21.explain: Akhā ʿĀd: Hūd, one of their own. He warned them at al-Aḥqāf, long curving sand dunes, reportedly in Yemen. Warners came before and after him with one message: worship only Allah.

22.explain: They said: have you come li-taʾfikanā, to turn us away from our gods? Then bring the punishment you threaten, if you are truthful. They demanded it, not believing it would ever come.

23.explain: Hūd: al-ʿilmu ʿinda Allāh, only Allah knows when it comes. I just deliver what I was sent with. But you are a people acting ignorantly, daring to rush the punishment.

24.explain: They saw a ʿāriḍ, a cloud spread across the sky, heading for their drought-struck valleys, and cheered: rain! No, it was what they had rushed: a wind carrying a painful punishment.

25.explain: It destroyed everything it was sent against, by its Lord’s command. By morning only their empty homes could be seen; Hūd and the believers were saved. Kadhālika: this is how criminals are repaid.

26.explain: Makkannāhum: ʿĀd were more firmly established than you, Makkah, with hearing, sight and hearts. None of it helped when they rejected Allah’s signs, and the punishment they mocked closed in on them.

27.explain: Allah destroyed towns around Makkah, like ʿĀd to the south and Thamūd and Lūṭ’s people to the north, near the trade routes. He set out the signs in many ways so they might turn back.

28.explain: Why didn’t the gods they took as qurbān, a way to get near Allah, help them? They vanished when needed most. That was their ifk, their lie, and what they invented.

29.explain: Allah turned a nafar, a small group, of jinn toward the Prophet ﷺ to hear the Qurʾān. They told each other anṣitū: be silent and listen. When it ended, they returned to their people as warners.
29.why: Reportedly jinn, blocked from eavesdropping on heaven, searched the earth and found the Prophet ﷺ leading Fajr at Nakhlah. Another report places it on his return from Ṭāʾif, praying at night. They were seven or nine, and he didn’t see them.

30.explain: They said: we heard a Book sent down after Mūsā, confirming what came before. It guides to the truth in belief and to a straight path in action. They named Mūsā, whose Torah was the main book of law.

31.explain: Ajībū dāʿiya Allāh: answer Allah’s caller, the Prophet ﷺ, and believe in him. Allah will forgive your sins (or some of them) and shield you from painful punishment. His message reached jinn as well as humans.

32.explain: Whoever doesn’t answer Allah’s caller can’t escape Him anywhere on earth and has no protector besides Him. Such people are in clear error. The jinn called with hope (31), then warning (32).

33.explain: Don’t they see? Allah created the heavens and earth and lam yaʿya, did not tire. Surely He can bring the dead to life. Balā: yes! He has power over everything.

34.explain: When deniers are brought to the Fire they are asked: is this not real? They say: balā, yes, by our Lord. The confession comes too late: taste the punishment for denying.

35.explain: Be patient like ulū al-ʿazm, the messengers of firm resolve, and don’t rush their punishment. When they see it, life will feel like an hour of a day. Balāgh: the message is delivered. Only the defiantly disobedient are destroyed.
35.why: One report says this ayah came on the day of Uḥud, telling the Prophet ﷺ to be patient as the resolute messengers were. The surah itself is Makkan.
